posts.title: Reverse engineering a keyboard PCB
posts.description: A few years back, I received a mechanical keyboard from my work – Sentry. It is a beautiful, massive brick of aluminum with a 75% layout. The board came with bluetooth, per-key LED , and key-mappings to switch modifier keys for windows and mac layouts. Initially, the board worked fantastic.

posts.title: Upgrading to from HTMX1 to HTMX4
posts.description: I recently saw the htmx 4 release announcement and wanted to give the upgrade a try. While, I’ve been following the project for many years, but docket was using HTMX 1.x. With the release of HTMX 4, I wanted to upgrade.

posts.title: Introducing Taskturbine
posts.description: Through most of 2025, I had been working on Sentry’s task platform. That system operates with pretty high throughput (~200,000 tasks/second), so I’m familiar with the challenges in operating big systems in this space. In November 2025, Armin published a post on Absurd and I was intrigued by the operational simplicity that ‘just Postgres’ could provide.
